title: A Geometry-Based View of Mahalanobis OOD Detection
claim: A single radial rescaling of features changes ID geometry and decision regions, so choosing its strength can reduce ID–OOD overlap.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, one per parameter value, contour heatmaps behind scatter
description: Four side-by-side 2D scatter plots, each titled with a different normalization exponent: β=-0.5, 0, 1.0 and 1.5. Each plot shows three point clusters, colored dark blue, pink and yellow for Classes 0, 1 and 2, drawn over a viridis-style contour heatmap of Mahalanobis decision regions. At β=-0.5 the clusters are spread out and the contours are broad and overlapping. At β=0 the original elongated clusters have rounded elliptical contours around them. At β=1.0 all points collapse onto a unit circle, and the background becomes radial wedges. At β=1.5 the points contract into a tight clump near the origin, and the background is mostly flat yellow-green. Thin gray arrows from the original positions to the mapped positions appear in the last two panels. The legend sits in the first panel, and the eye goes first to the colorful scatter and the circle in panel three.
caption: Effect of radially scaled ℓ2 normalization on feature geometry and Mahalanobis boundaries. Visualization in 2D of the induced geometry and the resulting Mahalanobis decision regions. Gray arrows indicate the radial mapping from the original to the transformed space. Larger β contracts feature norms and tightens clusters, producing more localized decision regions; smaller β expands norms and broadens them. Choosing β appropriately can reduce ID–OOD overlap and improve OOD detection.
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is critical for reliable deployment of vision models. Mahalanobis-based detectors remain strong baselines, yet their performance varies widely across modern pretrained representations, and it is unclear which properties of a feature space cause these methods to succeed or fail. We conduct a large-scale study across diverse foundation-model backbones and Mahalanobis variants. First, we show that Mahalanobis-style OOD detection is not universally reliable: performance is highly representation-dependent and can shift substantially with pretraining data and fine-tuning regimes. Second, we link this variability to in-distribution geometry and identify a two-term ID summary that consistently tracks Mahalanobis OOD behavior across detectors: within-class spectral structure and local intrinsic dimensionality. Finally, we treat normalization as a geometric control mechanism and introduce radially scaled $\ell_2$ normalization, $Ï_Î²(z)=z/\|z\|^Î²$, which preserves directions while contracting or expanding feature radii. Varying $Î²$ changes the radii while preserving directions, so the same quadratic detector sees a different ID geometry. We choose $Î²$ from ID-only geometry signals and typically outperform fixed normalization baselines.
